data.text:
**Summary of findings**

- WAN link on gw.lan is physically up and addressed: `ifconfig vtnet0` shows `UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,LOWER_UP`, inet `198.51.100.27`; `netstat -rn` has a default route via `198.51.100.1`; `arp -n` shows the next hop resolved (`198.51.100.1 at 00:17:10:9a:a3:96`). The DHCP lease in `/var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0` is still well within its term (renew 2026/3/5, expire 2026/3/6), so this is not an expired/lost lease.
- Yet `ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1` → **100% packet loss**: nothing beyond the modem's LAN side answers, while local LAN (vtnet1 / 10.20.0.0/16) still works — matching "local services still work".
- The watchdog records show what happened at onset: `/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl` logs `No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out` at 02:01:44 (upstream loss → modem fell out of sync), then `TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND` at 02:14:10, then `Cable Modem Reboot because of - unknown; registration complete` at 02:28:21.
- `modem-metrics.jsonl` confirms recovery on the radio/coax side: `NOT_SYNCHRONIZED` at 02:06 → `OPERATIONAL` from 02:29 with healthy plant figures (`min_snr 37.6–37.9 dB`). So the modem itself has re-synced and re-registered.
- Despite that, connectivity is still absent at 02:41, and the firewall's WAN has already been reconfigured twice during this outage: `state.json` shows `"reloads_in_outage": 2`, `"last_reload": 1772523600` (02:40), `"last_action": "reload"`. Two lease renewals did not restore anything.

**Interpretation:** the outage began with a provider-side upstream failure (ranging timeout) that forced the cable modem to reboot and re-register. The modem is now registered and operational, and the firewall's own WAN addressing/routing is intact, but traffic still dies at the provider boundary — the CPE/gateway does not respond even after two WAN renewals. That points beyond the modem, into the provider's network, rather than to the firewall's lease, NAT, routes or NIC.

data.cause: The ISP link dropped when the modem lost upstream ranging (T3 timeout) and the provider's network has still not restored service after the modem re-registered, so traffic dies beyond the modem even though the firewall's WAN addressing is valid.

data.recommendation: Report the outage to the ISP: their network stopped carrying our traffic after the modem's upstream loss and self-reboot at ~02:28, even though the modem now reports OPERATIONAL. Ask them to check the provisioning path (note the 'TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND' event) and the CPE/gateway at 198.51.100.1 that is not answering. No local change is needed; further WAN renewals will not help, since two have already been done in this outage. Keep the watchdog in observe mode until the provider confirms restoration.
data.detail: Provider side dead past the modem: modem re-registered but gateway/ISP unreachable
